rows.description: A child says they love an aunt's gift or a bland dish to avoid hurting her. The motive is care and belonging, and the child is learning that truth and kindness can pull in different directions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, nostalgia, hurt

rows.description: A teenager says they are fine, or that they liked a friend's poem, to dodge an awkward scene. Kindness mixes with cowardice, and the habit can quietly replace real closeness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who hears everything is great about a weak performance feels warm at first, then confused when results say otherwise. Praise that is never calibrated stops being usable information.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult tells many small polite falsehoods to friends and flatmates and starts to notice they no longer know who really likes them. Small kindnesses are fine, but a steady stream can hollow out trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Choosing a kind true sentence instead [Response]
rows.description: An adult replaces a false compliment with something both true and warm, such as saying they can see the effort put in. This keeps care and honesty together without lecturing anyone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child says the cousin broke the glass because they expect shouting or a slap. The lie is a panic move to escape a feared consequence, not a plan to deceive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Covering a mistake or bad marks [Actor]
rows.description: A schoolchild hides a low test score or forges a signature because shame feels bigger than the truth. Each cover-up needs another lie and grows the fear it was meant to end.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An adult stays calm, names the fear behind the lie, and makes the truth cheaper than the cover-up by thanking the child for telling it. Harsh punishment teaches better concealment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: gratitude, fear, calm

rows.description: A teenager hides a friendship or phone use because past honesty led to control or ridicule. The lie says more about how safe the truth felt than about the teenager's character.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A student in a high-expectation family claims good grades or a job offer while quietly failing. Fear of disappointing parents is real, and the gap between story and reality slowly becomes a trap.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
